relevance_note: Case series of three related patients with GFAP M451I: 'three patients with genetically confirmed AOAD from the same family'.
method_note: Read the whole paper by hand; a short Python script assembled the JSON and cut table spans from the Markdown lines, and each table-derived value was checked against Table 1 (patients as rows, label column 'Clinical findings') and Table 2 (patients as columns). Table 2's header row is garbled in the conversion ('| Case | 1 Case 2 | Case 3 |'); the three data columns are Case 1, Case 2 and Case 3, confirmed by the figure superscripts (A = case 1, B = case 2, C = case 3, per the Figure 2 legend). Neither table defines '+' or '-'; '+' cells were taken as present, and '-' cells were treated as not reported (no definition). Gd enhancement is nevertheless excluded for all three from the text 'none of our patients showed contrast enhancement' (group statement). Case 2's '-' for putamen/globus pallidus is left not reported; the abstract's 'Basal ganglia were affected in two cases' does not name Case 2 as unaffected. Table 1 empty cells are not reported; its '*initial symptom' row is a legend for the asterisk on urinary incontinence. The '>' in the Markdown is an HTML entity from conversion; spans keep '>', values use '>'. Inheritance for Cases 1 and 2 is 'inherited maternal' because Case 3 is stated to be their mother and to carry the same heterozygous M451I (c.1245G>A) mutation; no parental testing is reported for Case 3. The maternal grandmother of Case 1 (deceased, paraplegia after repetitive head trauma, not tested, not called affected) was included as a relative described in relation to Case 1; she has no variant row. Case 1's baby is mentioned but not described and has no row. Possible contradictions: (1) Case 1's cervical spinal cord is described in the text as atrophic 'although no prominent signal abnormalities were notes on T2W images', while Table 2 marks '+' for 'Atrophy and signal changes in the C1-C2 spinal cord'; both rows are emitted, and the checklist item is observed on atrophy, which both sources support. (2) The Discussion says symptoms in case 1 started 'following a severe multitrauma, including head injuries', whereas the case report places the fall 2 years after symptom onset at 33 years. (3) Case 3's onset is given as 56 years in the Discussion while she is 60 with vertigo for 5 years and urinary incontinence for 7 years. Case 2's onset is given only as '8 months ago' (not an age), so age at onset is not reported. Normal laboratory panels were recorded as excluded abnormalities under D-27. 'Dilated ventricles' was not mapped to the hydrocephalus checklist item, and the brainstem 'hyperintense rim' was not mapped to 'periventricular rim'. Rhinolalia (Cases 2 and 3) was mapped to 'dysarthria or dysphonia'; Case 3's positive Romberg and impaired tandem walk were mapped to 'ataxia or cerebellar signs'. The statement that detailed examination revealed no extrapyramidal findings does not name the patients it covers and was not used. Publication year is not printed in the document.
